text:
ashley: Heads-up — after the eu-west-1 rollout we see a spike in NAT egress from the inferencing cluster. Nodes are pulling model shards from our artifact registry but traffic is going out via NAT instead of the new interface endpoint :confused:

kyle: saw this in the cost dashboard, NAT bytes jumped ~2.4TB in the last 2 hours. Is PrivateLink actually attached to the subnets we use for GPU nodes?

maria: endpoint shows `Available` in console for com.redwood.artifacts, private DNS enabled. It's in 3 AZs and has SG rw-artifacts-ep-sg.

ashley: I ran a few checks — DNS inside pods resolves registry.redwood.internal -> private IPs from the VPCE hosted zone, but curl to those IPs still goes out via 10.0.1.1 (nat-gw) and times out intermittently.

dan: can you paste the coredns logs and iptables SNAT rules? quick suspicion: cluster DNS caching or iptables MASQUERADE hitting before endpoint ENI?

ashley: coredns logs show a cached A record ttl ~3000 on registry FQDN. iptables: 
```
-A POSTROUTING -s 10.244.0.0/16 ! -d 10.0.0.0/8 -j MASQUERADE
```
so SNAT is enabled for pod CIDR to anything outside 10.0.0.0/8 (our VPC range is 10.0.0.0/16)

kyle: that MASQUERADE rule would SNAT traffic destined to the endpoint's private IPs if endpoint IPs are in a different net? what IP range are the VPCE ENIs in?

maria: VPCE ENIs are in 172.31.0.0/20 — automation created them in a shared services account VPC via cross-account endpoint (long story).

dan: there you go. MASQUERADE is SNAT-ing pod traffic to node ip, then the endpoint SG only allows the original pod CIDR (10.244.0.0/16) and refuses the SNAT'd source, causing TCP handshake failures, so clients fall back to host-level retries which resolve public IPs or go via NAT.

ashley: great catch. So root causes: 1) coredns cached public mapping from before VPCE existed 2) SNAT rule masq'ing traffic to 172.31.x.x so SG drop 3) cross-account VPCE ENIs in different CIDR so iptables exception missing.

sre-bot: incident created #INC-2026-1872 and attached a short checklist.

maria: immediate mitigations I applied: added SG rule on rw-artifacts-ep-sg allowing source 10.244.0.0/16 and node IPs, and rolled a coredns restart to flush caches. Also added iptables exemption:
```
iptables -t nat -I POSTROUTING 1 -s 10.244.0.0/16 -d 172.31.0.0/20 -j ACCEPT
```

kyle: ran a quick curl from a pod to the private endpoint IP after that — TCP 200 within 120ms. NAT egress dropped ~1.8TB within 30 minutes. nice. :tada:

dan: longer-term fixes: 1) change iptables MASQUERADE rule to exclude all VPCE ranges (we'll generate a subnet list from endpoints), 2) update endpoint SG automation to include pod CIDR + node IPs at creation time, 3) ensure cross-account endpoints are created in VPC ranges that don't require SNAT special-casing if possible, 4) reduce TTLs during infra changes so coredns doesn't cache old A records for hours.

ashley: I'll open a PR with the iptables change and a small DaemonSet to manage the endpoint exception list on nodes. Also adding a pre-rollout checklist item: validate endpoint subnet CIDRs vs cluster SNAT rules.

maria: FYI ops-bot posted the rollout timeline earlier: `deploy-bot: rollout com/redwood/artifacts v3.2 -> eu-west-1 :rocket:` Noted that we enabled the endpoint in the middle of the deploy which probably triggered the mixed DNS state.

ops-bot: automation note: created aws-vpce-endpoint com.redwood.artifacts in eu-west-1 (3 azs).

ashley: cost note — preliminary estimate is ~12% lower egress spend for model downloads after the fix if this stays stable; if NAT had continued for another day we'd have seen sizable extra spend. I'll add a postmortem blurb to the incident.

kyle: one more thing — watch for conntrack churn on nodes while we roll the iptables change, might need graceful drain settings when updating the DaemonSet.

dan: verified endpoints by `dig +short registry.redwood.internal @10.0.0.2` -> returned 172.31.5.12 and `curl --interface 172.31.5.12 http://registry...` worked. All good.

ashley: thanks all — closing thread once the PR and DaemonSet are in prod. Will paste links to PR, incident, and cost dashboard in the doc. :thumbsup:
